analysis.title: Employment preview: September seasoning
key_insights: Barclays forecasts +50k nonfarm payroll gains in September for both headline and private payrolls, after June +31k, July +21k and August +162k. Government payrolls are expected to stay roughly flat.

Barring revisions, the 3-month average job gain for the three months ending September would be +78k/m, near the +81k/m pace for the three months ending June and well above the breakeven pace of around 0k/m.
Barclays expects the unemployment rate to stay at 4.1% amid low labor supply growth. It expects the FOMC to stay mindful of inconsistencies between the payroll and household surveys.
A flat unemployment rate and a modest payroll gain would keep an FOMC hold in play for October. Barclays then expects a 25bp rate hike in December.

Forecast uncertainty is elevated. Barclays' monthly models, built on weekly claims data, project strong gains because they extrapolate recent robust prints and weak initial claims since August's reference week. Its alternative indicator models point to more modest gains.

Barclays suspects the August payroll print of +162k will be revised down as the BLS extends its seasonal adjustment forward to include September data. With August 2025 seasonal factors, August would have shown a drop of 74k jobs instead of a 162k gain.

The August revision and September payrolls are linked. A larger downward revision to August would make September look stronger, which is an upside risk to the +50k forecast. Little revision to August would imply a weaker September than +50k.

Barclays expects average hourly earnings of +0.3% m/m (3.2% y/y) in September and a 0.1 hour decline in the workweek to 34.3 hours. This would likely show private payroll income declining after August's sharp increase.

Barclays expects a slight rise in the unemployment rate in August, from 4.090% to 4.141%, to be followed by a flat September reading. It retains a baseline that the unemployment rate trends lower through the end of 2026.

Barclays estimates August JOLTS job openings fell slightly to 7.200mn from 7.271mn. It says Indeed.com data and other sources suggest the current JOLTS level overstates labor demand, and it treats Indeed's weekly estimates as a better indicator of the underlying trend.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Barclays' forecast is modest job growth. It leaves the 3-month average at +78k, above the roughly 0k breakeven pace.
Barclays expects government payrolls to stay roughly flat, so private gains match the headline figure.
This assumes no revisions. It is near the +81k/m pace for the three months ending June and well above breakeven.
Barclays believes seasonal adjustment exaggerated this gain and expects a downward revision.
A flat rate would reflect continued divergence between the payroll and household surveys and would support an FOMC hold in October.
This was up slightly from 4.090% in July despite strong August payroll gains.
In line with the average pace over the past 12 months.
The pace is steady with the recent trend.
A 0.1 hour decline would likely show private payroll income falling after August's sharp rise.
A slight decline from 7.271mn, which Barclays attributes mostly to month-to-month measurement volatility.
This is the prior reading, which Barclays says likely overstates labor demand.
Barclays expects the FOMC to hold in October and then raise rates.

risk_factors: Seasonal adjustment may have exaggerated the August payroll gain. The size of the revision to August affects how strong September appears.
Barclays' monthly models and alternative indicator models send mixed signals, so uncertainty around the +50k forecast is elevated.
The payroll and household surveys disagree, which makes the labor market signal harder for the FOMC to read.
JOLTS has a limited sample size and may overstate labor demand.

tension_points.bull_case: If August is revised down substantially, September payrolls may appear stronger, which is an upside risk to the +50k forecast.
tension_points.bear_case: If August sees little downward revision, September payrolls may come in weaker than the +50k baseline.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The size of the August payroll revision when the BLS extends its seasonal adjustment forward with September data.
